description: Agent Reliability: submit a service’s published uptime report for a period with its incident and downtime log for the same period: the report with the service, the first and last days of the period, the availability it publishes, the downtime minutes it states and the incidents it counts; the log with the service, its period and each entry with its id, when the downtime began and ended and the minutes it records. The signed report gives the report and the log, the period in minutes, the availability recomputed from the log as the period less the logged downtime over the period and from the report’s own downtime, the downtime and the incident count on each side, and counts them, and names a misreported report: an availability above what the log supports, an availability that does not follow from the report’s own downtime over its period, fewer downtime minutes than the log records and fewer incidents than the log holds; then a lower availability, more downtime or incidents than the log, another period or service and log entries outside the period, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No availability, downtime or incident count in the report, no complete period, or a log entry with neither minutes nor a start and end time leaves the report unverified. Periods count whole days at 1,440 minutes a day, availability compares to the hundredth of a percentage point and minutes to the tenth. This reads records, never the service: wever_endpoint-reliability-check probes one live MCP or x402 endpoint and scores its reachability, TLS, latency and consistency, and wever_endpoint-honesty-check reads one live 402 challenge against its advertised price, both single-moment probes on the Endpoint reliability page, while the uptime check connects to nothing and reads a published report against the log for the same period; wever_sla-credit-check computes one month’s uptime from outage figures and names the service credit the terms prescribe, while the uptime check computes no credit and names no amount owed. Verdict rely_uptime_misreported, rely_uptime_partial, rely_uptime_unverified or rely_uptime_faithful. POST /api/rely-uptime-check. Reads the reliability records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never probes, pings or measures a live service or endpoint, computes no service credit and names no amount owed, verifies nothing with outside sources and judges no service’s actual reliability, only whether its records agree with each other and with what it advertises, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Reliability reads a service’s reliability records for consistency between documents: an uptime report, an error budget record, a failover arrangement, a dependency disclosure, a degradation behavior record, an incident history, a maintenance record and a periodic reliability report, each against the log, SLO, terms, listing, advertised behavior, buyer disclosure, policy or records it should agree with. Beside it, wever_endpoint-reliability-check and wever_endpoint-honesty-check probe one live endpoint at one moment for the Endpoint reliability page, and the DiligenceOps reads such as wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_status-evidence-check restate one document on its own, while this family connects to nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what the service advertises. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-reliability-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-reliability/.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

entries.description: Each incident or downtime entry in the log for the period.

minutes.description: The minutes of downtime the entry records.

started_at.description: When the downtime began, such as 2026-10-03T14:05:00Z.

period_from.description: The first day of the period, such as 2026-10-31.

period_to.description: The last day of the period, such as 2026-10-31.

name: wever_rely-uptime-check
title: Reliability uptime check
